headline: Benchmarked computational methods for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics analysis
label: Single Cell Computational Methods
summary: Single-cell and spatial omics pipelines now depend on validated annotation, imputation and benchmarking frameworks tested on simulated and real data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational methodology for single-cell and spatial profiling, where new tools are introduced and assessed against simulated or orthogonal ground truth. scATrans separates transcription from stabilization effects in single-cell differential expression using unspliced RNA and benchmarks against metabolic labeling. stCNASim provides an allele-aware spatial RNA-seq simulator for benchmarking five copy-number inference methods across 46 synthetic datasets. Other entries address cell annotation (Binary-SPA, CELLIA), imputation for single-cell proteomics (SoftHybrid), pathway scoring (scROMA, pysigscore), highly variable gene selection (Principal Genes), and background correction in multiplex spatial proteomics (bgnorm). What is new is the emphasis on validation frameworks and on uncertainty or interpretability, though these represent heterogeneous contributions rather than a single shared advance.
